# Best Portable Power Stations for Camping

The right size depends on your camping style. For most tent and car camping, a **~300 Wh LiFePO4 unit** covers phones, lights, a fan, and even a CPAP for several nights, and it stays light enough to carry one-handed. If you want to run a 12V fridge or camp out of a van, step up to about 1 kWh.

## Weekend tent and car camping (~300 Wh class)

| Pick | Capacity / AC output | Weight | Approx. price | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (best overall) | 288 Wh / 300 W | ~8.3 lb | ~$249 | Lightest and simplest of the group, and it pairs easily with Jackery solar panels |
| **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (best value) | 286 Wh / 600 W | ~9.9 lb | ~$269–299 | Double the inverter output, and an add-on battery expands it to 572 Wh |
| **Anker SOLIX C300** (long trips) | 288 Wh / 300 W | ~9.3 lb | ~$199 | Built-in pop-up lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the AC version, not the "C300 DC." |
| **Bluetti EB3A** (budget) | 268 Wh / 600 W | ~10.1 lb | ~$179 | The cheapest real LiFePO4 option |

Source and retailer links: [PowerStationGearLab camping guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

Jackery's own site has replaced the 300 Plus with the **Explorer 300 v2**, which charges faster but has a shorter warranty. The Plus is still sold on Amazon. A CPAP tip: turning the humidifier off can stretch a 300 Wh unit to 3–5 nights.

## Van life, fridges, or bigger setups (~1 kWh and up)

- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**: 1,070 Wh, 1,500 W, ~23.8 lb, ~$799. TechRadar and PowerStationGearLab both pick it as their camping or overland choice. ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's best value pick, recently on sale for under $530. It weighs 25 lb and delivered 890 Wh in their testing, though its fan is noisy. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **BLUETTI AC180**: 1,152 Wh LiFePO4 with an 1,800 W inverter and a 5-year warranty. It costs $499, or $474.05 with code **AFF5OFF**, which was tested at checkout on 10/21. It's heavy at about 35 lb and can't be expanded. [Buy at BLUETTI](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). This is an affiliate link from [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180).
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: WIRED's camping pick. It's IP65 weatherproof and drop-resistant, with 1,536 Wh, for ~$1,079 on sale. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/))
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: OutdoorGearLab's choice for multi-day off-grid trips. It has 2,042 Wh, weighs 39 lb, and has been under $900 on Amazon.

## My quick recommendation

- **Charging devices, lights, and a CPAP:** get the Jackery 300 Plus, or the EcoFlow River 3 Plus if you want more output.
- **Running a 12V fridge or a van setup:** get the Jackery 1000 v2 or the Anker C1000 Gen 2.

Black Friday is close, so prices on all of these will likely drop soon. Most of the review links above go to Amazon or other retailers, and many of them earn affiliate commissions.

What will you be powering, and is this tent or car camping? Tell me and I can narrow it to one pick.
